headline: Kavinsky's family breaks silence: "keep his music alive"
standfirst: After four months of silence, Kavinsky's family has spoken for the first time and pledged to "keep his music alive", DJ Mag reports.
body: Four months after his death, Kavinsky's family has broken its silence with a pledge to "keep his music alive", DJ Mag reports.
The French producer died in July at the age of 50.
He is best known for 'Nightcall', the track that became a hit through the film Drive.
The family's message is short. Its focus is his music, and keeping it going.

headline: Lisbon coffee rave brings shelter dogs to the floor
standfirst: Sundaze Morning Social returns this Sunday, 29 November, with "Paws On The Dance Floor": 11:00 to 14:00 at Connection Studio, Rua da Bempostinha, Lisbon. Ønawa and DJ Breadbox play together across deep house, afro house and tech house, and a welcome coffee comes with the ticket.
body: Lisbon's coffee rave scene has a new kind of guest list. On Sunday, 29 November, Sundaze Morning Social brings its morning party to Connection Studio on Rua da Bempostinha with a special edition called "Paws On The Dance Floor". It runs from 11:00 to 14:00, and dogs from the Lisbon animal protection association União Zoófila will be there looking for new homes.

Ønawa and DJ Breadbox play a joint set. Expect deep house, afro house and tech house. The bar runs on caffeine rather than spirits: a welcome coffee is included in the ticket. The idea is a party for people who love music and want to meet new people but would rather keep their mornings than lose their nights.

The dogs arrive in the final hour, from 13:00 to 14:00. You can meet them, play with them and find out more about the association. The event is organised with LivFest Portugal and aims to promote responsible adoption and give some visibility to animals still waiting for a family.
If you want to help, you can bring dog or cat food, donate money at the event or give directly to União Zoófila.

Sundaze Morning Social isn't new to this. The project turned one in June with a rooftop party at IDB Rooftop by Mīrārī in Marvila that mixed music with running and Pilates. This time it swaps the terrace for a café setting and adds a good cause.

Tickets are on sale online from €10, and late entry costs €12. Coffee raves keep growing in Lisbon, and this one is a reminder that the daytime crowd has its own rituals. Not every great pista needs a 6am finish.

headline: Viseu techno night gives all profits to firefighters
standfirst: Electronic Beira Sounds, a techno event organised by Dark Waves, takes over the Pavilhão Multiusos de Viseu this Saturday.
body: Viseu gets a techno night this Saturday, and the whole profit goes to charity. Electronic Beira Sounds, organised by Dark Waves, takes over the Pavilhão Multiusos de Viseu, and every euro of profit goes to the Associação Humanitária de Bombeiros Voluntários de Viseu, the city's volunteer fire brigade.
The lineup is techno all night: Cravo b2b Vil, Du/art, Frank Maurel, Valody and Tryängle b2b VASQ.

The organisers have planned more than a stage and a dancefloor. There will be a bar, a food court and a chill out zone. There will also be a besafe space that raises awareness of risky behaviour. Harm reduction like this is still not standard at Portuguese events, and seeing it at a regional party is a good sign.

There's also a Creative HUB where local artists will give demos and sell their work. Add flash tattoos, a make-up artist, a hairdresser, crafts, custom t-shirts and a graffiti artist painting at the entrance, and it feels closer to a small festival than a normal club night.

The Município de Viseu supports the event through its Eixo Cultura programme. That matters. Electronic music outside Lisbon and Porto often has to fight for venues and recognition, and here a city hall is backing a techno event in a municipal pavilion.
For ravers in the Centro region, it's a reason to stay close to home this weekend. Everyone else should take note: the interior is building its own nights, and they come with a conscience.

points.title: Where the money goes
points.text: 100% of the profits go to Viseu's volunteer firefighters, the Associação Humanitária de Bombeiros Voluntários de Viseu.

points.title: Harm reduction on site
points.text: A besafe space will raise awareness of risky behaviour, next to a chill out zone, a bar and a food court.

points.title: More than a dancefloor
points.text: The Creative HUB has local artists doing demos and selling their work, plus flash tattoos, a make-up artist, a hairdresser, crafts, custom t-shirts and a graffiti painter at the entrance.

headline: Hannah Laing: from dental nurse to the doof
standfirst: Weekdays at the dental clinic, weekends on tour: Hannah Laing did both for 10 years. After a well-received Creamfields set in 2022, the Dundee DJ quit nursing and went full-time. She called the move "terrifying and freeing".
body: For ten years, Hannah Laing worked as a dental nurse during the week and toured at weekends. After a well-received set at Creamfields in 2022 she quit, and she has described going full-time as "terrifying and freeing". The Dundee DJ and producer now runs her own label, Doof, and her own festival.

Laing was born in Dundee in 1994. Her parents got her into rave music, and she played her first gig at 18 in an Arbroath venue. Fun fact: in 2007 she competed on CBBC's Raven and came fifth in the first week. While still nursing, she also held a DJ residency in San Antonio.

BBC Radio 1 helped her break through. Pete Tong and Danny Howard picked up on her, she played Radio 1's Big Weekend in 2022, and she headlined its dance stage in 2023. She has also recorded a two-hour Essential Mix. Her 2019 remix of Sophie Ellis-Bextor's Murder on the Dancefloor was played in DJ sets around the world. In 2023, Good Love with RoRo spent 26 weeks in the UK Singles Chart, peaked at number 7 and went Platinum. She has played TRNSMT, Creamfields and the Tidy Weekender, and she supported Idris Elba in Ibiza.

She calls her sound "doof", after the doof doof beat. The Into the Doof EP came out in July 2024. It was made over three days with other DJs, and she said it reflects "all the different styles I love". In July 2025 she launched Doof in the Park at Camperdown Country Park in Dundee. Around 15,000 people came, and Armin van Buuren, Judge Jules and Lisa Lashes were on the lineup. The festival returns in 2026.

That same year she held a residency at Hï Ibiza and released the Into the Bounce EP. In November 2025 she released Have You Ever Loved (Ellie), a tribute to her best friend, who had died earlier that year. It was her third Radio 1 Hottest Record, after Good Love and FWTDJ.

points.title: The sound
points.text: High-energy hard house, trance and techno, which she calls "doof" after the doof doof beat. She has played the Tidy Weekender and appears on TDV25 - The Remixes, the Tidy Trax tribute to hard house pioneer Tony De Vit.

points.title: Why now
points.text: In 2025 she launched Doof in the Park in Dundee (around 15,000 people, back in 2026), held a Hï Ibiza residency and released the Into the Bounce EP. Before that came a two-hour Essential Mix and a 2023 Big Weekend dance-stage headline.

points.title: Start here
points.text: Good Love with RoRo (26 weeks in the UK chart, peaked at No. 7, Platinum), her 2019 Murder on the Dancefloor remix, the Into the Doof EP, and Have You Ever Loved (Ellie), her tribute to her late best friend.

headline: Josh Baker and Cloonee close Primavera Sound Porto
standfirst: Primavera Sound Porto has split its 55 names across four days for its 14th edition, 10–13 June at Parque da Cidade. Sunday is electronic only again: Primavera Bits, with Josh Baker, Cloonee, Carlita and Trikk.
body: Primavera Sound Porto has said which day each act plays at its 14th edition. The 55 names are spread over 10 to 13 June next year at Parque da Cidade. As before, there are three days of concerts, and the Sunday belongs to electronic music. That Sunday is Primavera Bits on 13 June, and Josh Baker, Cloonee, Carlita and Trikk will play it.

Bits is also the cheapest day of the weekend. A Sunday ticket costs 40€, while each of the three concert days costs 80€. The four-day pass is 190€ and VIP is 300€, before booking fees. Tickets are on sale online now.

If you're coming for the dancefloor, Saturday 12 June is worth a look too. FKA twigs and The Chemical Brothers top the bill. Metronomy, CHVRCHES and Wilco play the same day, along with Christine and the Queens, Shygirl and Simian Mobile Disco.

Thursday 10 June has Fontaines D.C. and Lola Young at the top, with Tinashe, Theodora and Dinosaur Jr also playing. On Friday 11 June the headliners are Hayley Williams, beabadoobee, Kim Petras and Bleachers, and ANOHNI, Converge and DIIV are also on.

There are plenty of Portuguese acts. Cassete Pirata and Mães Solteiras open the festival on Thursday. Branko plays Friday, along with Bia Soull, 800 Gondomar and A Sul. Clã, PZ and MAQUINA play Saturday.
For club people, the order of the weekend matters. Three days of bands and pop come first, and the electronic day comes last, at half the price.

points.title: The Bits maths
points.text: Primavera Bits costs 40€, half the price of each of the three concert days. If Sunday is the only day you want, it's the cheapest way into the Parque da Cidade weekend.

points.title: Saturday for dancers
points.text: Saturday 12 June has the most electronic acts outside Bits: The Chemical Brothers and FKA twigs headline, with Simian Mobile Disco, Shygirl and Christine and the Queens also on the bill.

points.title: The Portuguese contingent
points.text: Cassete Pirata and Mães Solteiras play Thursday. Branko, Bia Soull, 800 Gondomar and A Sul play Friday. Clã, PZ and MAQUINA play Saturday.

headline: DJ Marfox took his name from Star Fox
standfirst: DJ Marfox, born Marlon Silva in Lisbon in June 1988 to parents from São Tomé e Príncipe, is best known for pioneering batida, the "ghetto sound of Lisbon" that mixes kuduro, kizomba, funaná and tarraxinha with house and techno.
body: Before he was one of the names that took Lisbon's sound around the world, DJ Marfox was a teenager playing Nintendo. The name joins "Marl", from his first name Marlon, with Star Fox, the character he played growing up.

Marlon Silva was born in Lisbon in June 1988 to parents from São Tomé e Príncipe and started deejaying as DJ Marfox in 2002. He is best known for pioneering batida, or batucada, the "ghetto sound of Lisbon" that came out of the city's housing estates and mixes African-influenced dance music such as kuduro, kizomba, funaná and tarraxinha with house and techno.

The scene's founding document wasn't pressed on vinyl. In 2005 he founded DJs do Guetto with DJ Pausas and DJ Fofuxo, and a year later they released DJs do Ghetto Vol. I, a 37-track digital compilation, on eMule. Príncipe Discos later re-issued it as a free download, and it is seen as the foundational release of the ghetto sound of Lisbon.

Príncipe also released his first solo album, Eu sei quem Eu Sou (I Know Who I Am), in early 2011. Philip Sherburne described it as "an atomic field of taut drums, hiccupping yelps, zapping synths and pinprick details."

In 2014 came the Lucky Punch EP on Lit City Trax, a Red Bull Music Academy performance in New York and a Warm Up show at MoMA PS1 on 30 August 2014. Rolling Stone also put him on its list of "10 New Artists You Need to Know".

In 2015 the bedroom tracks he made between 2005 and 2008 came out as Revolução 2005–2008, and WARP released Cargaa 1, an EP with DJ Marfox as its central figure. From a gamer tag and an eMule upload to one of Britain's best-known electronic labels, it's a very Lisbon story.

points.title: Named after Star Fox
points.text: 'Marfox' joins 'Marl', from Marlon, with Star Fox, the Nintendo character he played as a teenager. One of Lisbon's most important DJ names started as a gamer tag.

points.title: The scene began on eMule
points.text: In 2006, DJs do Guetto, the crew he founded with DJ Pausas and DJ Fofuxo, put DJs do Ghetto Vol. I on eMule: 37 tracks. It's seen as the foundational release of Lisbon's ghetto sound.

points.title: From bedroom to WARP
points.text: Tracks he made in his bedroom from 2005 to 2008 came out as Revolução 2005–2008 in 2015. That same year WARP put him at the centre of its Cargaa 1 EP.

headline: Disclosure remixer RIVO opens Sodade's new Lisbon series
standfirst: please do not disturb, a new concept from promoter Sodade, debuts 19 December at LX Factory. Headliner RIVO broke out with his 2024 remix of Disclosure's 'You & Me', then made 'Last Night' and 'Like A Dream' with Adriatique and 'In & Out of Love' with Armin van Buuren. 700M+ streams.
body: French DJ and producer RIVO headlines the first edition of please do not disturb, a new electronic music event concept from promoter Sodade, on 19 December at LX Factory in Lisbon. Three more names have now joined the bill: Portuguese duo Mayze x Faria, French artist Max Arthur and Portuguese DJ JÖAH.

RIVO broke through internationally in 2024 with his remix of Disclosure's 'You & Me'. Releases with Armin van Buuren ('In & Out of Love') and Adriatique ('Last Night', 'Like A Dream') followed. He has passed 700 million streams and played more than 250 shows, including Tomorrowland Belgium, Hï Ibiza, Ushuaïa Ibiza, Drumsheds London, Lollapalooza Paris and Ultra Miami. In Portugal he played Nómadas festival, where he shared the stage with fadista Bia Caboz in a moment that went viral.

Sodade pitches the project as more than a new party series. Its motto is "disconnect to connect. please do not disturb": the crowd is asked to set aside everyday distractions and focus on the music, the artist and the moment. Each edition is planned as a standalone experience, with music, space, lighting, production and visuals designed together and adapted to each venue.

Mayze x Faria, Jonh Mayze and Miguel Faria, formed in Braga in 2004 and work across melodic techno, melodic house and tech house. They have played in Spain, Luxembourg, Colombia, Angola, Brazil and Mexico, and won the Talent Award from Portuguese platform 100% DJ in 2021.

Max Arthur was DJing at 10 and was billed as France's youngest DJ and producer. He returned in 2024 after more than a decade away with a new project blending house, indie dance and melodic house, and has since played Ibiza, Mykonos, Paris, Brussels and Geneva.
JÖAH is the founder and resident of Soulset, with sets moving through house, tech house and afro-house at venues around Lisbon and in Vilamoura. Tickets are on sale at sodade.bol.pt.

headline: Lisbon's Joe Delon steps up for DJ Mag's Recognise
standfirst: Lisbon-based DJ and label boss Joe Delon has recorded a two-hour mix for DJ Mag's Recognise series, now at episode 121. It moves through decades of house music.
body: Joe Delon, the Lisbon-based DJ and label boss, has recorded the 121st episode of DJ Mag's Recognise series. It's a two-hour mix that covers decades of house music.
DJ Mag describes the selection as punchy, playful and emotive. The magazine says it shows the disco-rooted approach to the dancefloor that has guided Delon through 20 years of DJing.

Delon founded the label Welt Discos. With the mix comes a conversation with writer Michael McKinney about his feelings-first ethos, what ambiguity adds to a DJ set, and his push against narrow definitions of queer dance music. They also talk about jigsaw puzzles.

For readers in Portugal, it's a Lisbon DJ getting two full hours and a long-form interview on one of electronic music's biggest international platforms. Mix series like Recognise are one way selectors reach listeners far from their home city, and this one puts a Lisbon name in that spotlight.
The mix and the full interview are on DJ Mag's website as part of the Recognise series.

headline: Integrador Dimensional: Nicolas Lutz goes vinyl-only
standfirst: Nicolas Lutz has launched Integrador Dimensional, a vinyl-only label co-founded with Fabiola Andriolo, Head of Projects at Polifonic.
body: Nicolas Lutz has launched Integrador Dimensional, a new record label that will release music only on vinyl. He co-founded it with Fabiola Andriolo, Head of Projects at Polifonic.
The first record is 'Dharma Effect' by Nicolas Etorena, a producer born in Uruguay and based in Barcelona. It comes out on 15 January 2027, and pre-orders opened on 24 November 2026.
Integrador Dimensional is not built around a signature sound. The label aims to bring distinct musical identities together through shared sensibilities rather than a uniform sound.

For Lutz and Andriolo, the concept centres on intuition, curiosity and the relationships that can form between musical expressions that are otherwise different. So the catalogue is meant to grow through connections between artists, not around a genre template.
The format is part of that identity. With 'Dharma Effect' as its first release, Integrador Dimensional is starting out as a physical-format imprint that releases only on vinyl.
'Dharma Effect' can be heard with the label's announcement, and pre-orders are open now ahead of the January release.

headline: Jamaica Suk, Berlin techno's "gentle soul", has died
standfirst: Jamaica Suk, the Berlin techno DJ, producer and label founder, has died, Mixmag reports.
body: Jamaica Suk, the Berlin techno DJ, producer and label founder, has died, Mixmag reports.
Tributes remember her as a “wonderful, gentle soul”, someone who uplifted the people around her.
Her work covered the booth, the studio and the label side of the scene, and the words chosen to remember her are about how she treated other people.
HARDMAG sends its condolences to her family, her friends and everyone who knew her, played alongside her or danced to her music. Rest in peace, Jamaica.

headline: TIDAL to ban AI-generated tracks "entirely" next month
standfirst: TIDAL says it will ban AI-generated tracks "entirely" next month, per Mixmag.
body: TIDAL says it will ban AI-generated tracks from its platform "entirely" next month, Mixmag reports. The word "entirely" is the streaming service's own, quoted in Mixmag's headline.

The ban follows an earlier step. TIDAL says that since July it has labelled and demonetised 100% of all AI tracks on the platform. In other words, AI-generated music was marked as such and earned nothing.
A ban is a different kind of policy. Labelling and demonetising tells listeners what they are hearing and stops payments. A ban says this music isn't allowed on the service at all.

What the ban covers in practice isn't spelled out in the material available. It doesn't say whether tracks already on TIDAL will be taken down or whether the rule only applies to new uploads, or how TIDAL defines and detects an AI-generated track.

For producers and labels distributing music to TIDAL, including the many independent artists in Portugal who release through digital distributors, it's worth watching the details when the policy takes effect next month.

headline: Kettama: from a Galway Launchpad to Radio 1
standfirst: Kettama is Evan Campbell, an Irish producer and DJ born in Galway in 1997. At 16 he bought a Launchpad, got an Ableton trial with it and taught himself by remaking the piano from Tyga's "I'm Different". Six months later he was on cracked FL Studio, uploading to SoundCloud.
body: Kettama, the Galway producer and DJ born Evan Campbell in 1997, has held a BBC Radio 1 Dance residency since 2025. On 29 May 2026 his single "Comes and Goes" entered the Irish Singles Chart at No. 19 and climbed to the top of the Irish Homegrown Chart.

He started out teaching himself. At 16, Campbell bought a Launchpad that came with an Ableton trial and experimented by remaking the piano from Tyga's "I'm Different". Six months later he downloaded a cracked copy of FL Studio and began uploading tracks to SoundCloud. By 17 he was playing clubs.

His breakthrough came in 2018 with "B O D Y", from the Bucklyn Bridge EP. It reached an international audience after Mall Grab and fellow Irish DJ Annie Mac played it often. A year later he co-founded G-Town Records with Shampain and named the label after Galway, the hometown they share.
Alongside his solo work, he performs and releases under collaborative aliases: Samba Boys with Tommy Holohan, and KETBOI69, a portmanteau project with Partiboi69.

In 2023 he played a sold-out homecoming show during the Galway International Arts Festival. In 2024 he made his debuts at Glastonbury, Coachella and Boomtown. On 5 June 2025, "It Gets Better (Forever Mix)" charted at No. 37 on the Irish Singles Chart, a year before "Comes and Goes" entered higher.
If you're new to him, start with "B O D Y", the track that broke him, then play "It Gets Better (Forever Mix)" and "Comes and Goes" to hear where his music has gone since.

points.title: The breakthrough
points.text: "B O D Y", from the 2018 Bucklyn Bridge EP, took him international after frequent play from Mall Grab and fellow Irish DJ Annie Mac.

points.title: From Galway to Glastonbury
points.text: In 2019 he co-founded G-Town Records with Shampain, named after their hometown. He sold out a 2023 homecoming show at the Galway International Arts Festival, then debuted at Glastonbury, Coachella and Boomtown in 2024.

points.title: Why now
points.text: In 2025 he became a BBC Radio 1 Dance resident and "It Gets Better (Forever Mix)" hit No. 37 on the Irish Singles Chart. In May 2026 "Comes and Goes" entered at No. 19 and topped the Irish Homegrown Chart.

headline: SoundCloud cracks down on AI slop and spam
standfirst: SoundCloud is cracking down on what it calls "AI slop, spam, and excessive uploads", according to Music Business Worldwide.
body: SoundCloud is cracking down on what it calls "AI slop, spam, and excessive uploads", Music Business Worldwide reports. The platform has introduced new terms aimed at users who use AI to game its systems.

Under the updated terms, SoundCloud can withhold, reverse or recover payouts from those users. That covers the whole payment cycle: money can be held back before it is paid, cancelled, or recovered after it has already been paid out.

The timing stands out. The crackdown comes only weeks after SoundCloud struck AI deals with Moises and ElevenLabs. So the platform is partnering with AI companies on one side and setting financial penalties for AI misuse on the other.

SoundCloud has long been a home base for DJs and producers sharing tracks, edits and mixes. For anyone earning money from uploads there, the new terms tie payouts directly to how the platform's systems are used. Using AI to game those systems can now put that income at risk.

The three targets named in the crackdown are AI slop, spam and excessive uploads. Those are problems streaming services across the industry are trying to deal with as AI-generated audio becomes cheaper and faster to make.

headline: Pete Tha Zouk: Locomia to DJ Mag's No. 37
standfirst: On 20 October 2011, Pete Tha Zouk climbed 44 places in the DJ Mag Top 100, from 81 to 37. No Portuguese DJ had ever placed higher.
body: On 20 October 2011, Pete Tha Zouk was announced at number 37 in the DJ Mag Top 100. He had entered the chart at 81 the year before, so he climbed 44 places. It was the highest position a Portuguese DJ had ever reached.

His education came from the booth. António Pedro was born in Olhão in 1978 and started as a resident at two venues: Mitto, a bar that changed how the South starts its nights, and Locomia, the seafront club on Santa Eulália beach. All the world's best-known DJs played Locomia during the summer seasons, and Pete got to watch them work up close.

His first tracks, 'First Tribal Feeling' with Bruno Marciano and 'Kashmira', were big dancefloor hits in the early 2000s. 'First Tribal Feeling' caught the attention of Chus, and soon afterwards Pete was in Madrid mastering it at the Chus & Ceballos studio. 'Kashmira' and 'Enchantments' followed and made his name as a producer for the floor.

In 2003 he and DJ Vibe released 'Solid Textures' on Low Pressings. The track topped the charts, and at the 2004 Dance Club awards it won Single of the Year while Pete was named Best Producer. The same magazine had named him DJ Revelação in 2002.

In 2006 he joined the agency WDB, which took his career to Brazil, Switzerland and Angola. His first gig outside Portugal was New Year 2010/11 in Brazil. In 2010 he released 'Check This Out' on Sondos, Erick Morillo's label, and that same year made his DJ Mag Top 100 debut at 81.

points.title: The WDB years
points.text: He joined WDB in 2006 and became Portugal's most in-demand DJ. Promoters knew his name meant 'casa cheia', a full house. WDB then took him to Brazil, Switzerland and Angola.

points.title: The awards
points.text: In 2004 Dance Club named him Best Producer and gave 'Solid Textures' Single of the Year. He won Melhor DJ Português at the Prémios Noite.pt in 2005, 2006, 2008, 2009 and 2010.

points.title: Start here
points.text: 'First Tribal Feeling' (with Bruno Marciano), 'Kashmira', 'Solid Textures' (2003, with DJ Vibe, Low Pressings), 'Check This Out' (2010, Erick Morillo's Sondos), 'I'm Back Again' (2010, with Mastercris and Abigail Bailey).

headline: Branko: the Lisbon producer wiring up global club music
standfirst: Branko, the alias of Portuguese DJ and producer João Barbosa, built his 2015 debut album Atlas from travels around Cape Town, New York, Amsterdam and São Paulo. Princess Nokia, DJ Sliink and Rodes Rollins all appear on it.
body: Branko is the solo name of João Barbosa, a Portuguese DJ and producer born on 28 November 1980. His records connect club music from several continents, and his label and radio show are run out of Lisbon. He first became known as part of Buraka Som Sistema and previously went by J-Wow.

His debut album as Branko, Atlas, came out in 2015. It was inspired by his travels around Cape Town, New York, Amsterdam and São Paulo, and featured Princess Nokia and DJ Sliink, plus Rodes Rollins on "Out Of Sight (So Right)".

The network kept growing. "Let Me Go", with Mr. Carmack and Nonku Phiri, was picked up by i-D, Hypebeast and The Fader. Rolling Stone announced his second solo album, Nosso, on 22 January 2019. Its guests include Sango, Cosima, Mallu Magalhães, Dino d'Santiago, Catalina García of Monsieur Periné, Pierre Kwenders, Miles From Kinshasa, Umi Copper, PEDRO and Dengue Dengue Dengue. Outside his own releases, he worked with M.I.A. on her 2016 album AIM and has also worked with Santigold and Anik Khan.

Lisbon is the base for all of it. Branko hosts Enchufada Na Zona, a monthly show on NTS broadcast live from the Lisbon headquarters of the label Enchufada. The show inspired a compilation of the same name. In 2018 he was also one of the interval acts at the Eurovision Song Contest final in Lisbon.
His most recent chapter came in 2024, when he released the single "Slide" featuring Jay Prince, building up to the release of his album SOMA in March that year.

points.text: "Let Me Go" with Mr. Carmack and Nonku Phiri got picked up by i-D, Hypebeast and The Fader. Nosso (2019) brought in Dengue Dengue Dengue, Catalina García of Monsieur Periné, Dino d'Santiago and PEDRO.

points.text: In 2024 he released "Slide" with Jay Prince, building up to the release of his album SOMA in March that year.

headline: DJ Nigga Fox and Príncipe's disorienting polyrhythms
standfirst: Rogério Brandão Luís was born in Luanda in 1990 and moved to Lisbon at four. He made his first beats on a computer in his bedroom on the city's outskirts.
body: DJ Nigga Fox has taken the disorienting polyrhythms of Lisbon's Afro-Portuguese diaspora from Lux Frágil, Musicbox, Iminente and Porto's Hard Club to Berghain, Sónar, Club to Club, H0L0 in New York and WWW in Tokyo. Príncipe discovered him and started releasing his music in 2011. Since then Rogério Brandão Luís has become one of the leading artists to emerge from Portugal's Afro-descendant communities.

He was born in Luanda in 1990 to a Congolese mother and an Angolan father, and moved to Lisbon with his parents and older brother at four. He grew up on the outskirts of the city and started building beats and melodies on a computer in his bedroom.
His music starts from kuduro, afro house, tarraxinha and batida and pushes them into experimental polyrhythms. Pitchfork, The Wire and Trax Magazine have all recognised his work more than once.

Wider attention came in stages. In early 2015, when few people knew Príncipe or its releases, Thom Yorke of Radiohead shared a list of tracks he was listening to. It included "Weed" alongside producers like Kool A.D. and Bernard Parmegiani. In 2016, British filmmakers Tim & Barry premiered "Sons do Gueto", a documentary about Príncipe and the African-influenced electronic music made in Lisbon's suburbs and social housing estates. It presented him as one of the label's faces.

He has also worked in film. He contributed to the soundtracks of Pedro Costa's "Vitalina Varela" and Rita Maia and Vasco Viana's "Batida de Lisboa", and his music was part of the opening of Copenhagen's CPH:DOX festival in 2020.

His Warp Records debut came in 2014 with "LUMI" on the CARGAA 1 compilation, followed by Crânio in 2018. On Príncipe, his catalogue runs from O Meu Estilo EP (2013) through Noite E Dia (2015) and 15 Barras (2017) to Cartas Na Manga (2019).

points.title: The Yorke moment
points.text: In early 2015, when few people knew Príncipe or its releases, Thom Yorke of Radiohead shared tracks he was listening to. Among them was "Weed", on a list with producers like Kool A.D. and Bernard Parmegiani.

points.title: On screen
points.text: In 2016, British filmmakers Tim & Barry's documentary "Sons do Gueto" presented him as one of Príncipe's faces. In 2020, his soundtrack work for "Vitalina Varela" and "Batida de Lisboa" was part of CPH:DOX's opening.

points.title: Start here
points.text: O Meu Estilo EP (2013), Noite E Dia (2015), 15 Barras (2017) and Cartas Na Manga (2019) on Príncipe, plus Crânio (2018) on Warp Records.

headline: From eMule to MoMA PS1: DJ Marfox and Lisbon's batida
standfirst: Born Marlon Silva in Lisbon in June 1988 to parents from São Tomé e Príncipe, DJ Marfox is credited with pioneering batida, the "ghetto sound of Lisbon" that came out of the city's housing estates. It fuses kuduro, kizomba, funaná and tarraxinha with house and techno.
body: DJ Marfox, born Marlon Silva in Lisbon in June 1988 to parents from São Tomé e Príncipe, is best known for pioneering batida, the "ghetto sound of Lisbon" that came out of the city's housing estates. It fuses African-influenced dance music such as kuduro, kizomba, funaná and tarraxinha with house and techno.

He has DJed as Marfox since 2002. The name joins "Marl" from Marlon with Star Fox, a Nintendo character he played as a teenager. In 2005 he founded DJs do Guetto with DJ Pausas and DJ Fofuxo. A year later the crew put DJs do Ghetto Vol. I, a 37-track digital compilation, on eMule. Príncipe Discos has since reissued it as a free download, and it is seen as the founding release of the ghetto sound of Lisbon.

His first solo album, Eu sei quem Eu Sou (I Know Who I Am), came out on Príncipe Discos in early 2011. Philip Sherburne described it as "an atomic field of taut drums, hiccupping yelps, zapping synths and pinprick details." Artist Unknown (Pollinaire, 2012) and Subliminar (Enchufada, 2013) followed.

In 2014 his Lucky Punch EP on Lit City Trax made Dazed's top ten albums for August. He played Red Bull Music Academy in New York, and on 30 August he played MoMA PS1's Warm Up series. Rolling Stone also named him among its "10 New Artists You Need to Know" that year. Cedar Pasori wrote that the PS1 appearance "reinforced the accelerating spread of Afro-Portuguese dance music around the world."

On 13 March 2015 Warp announced the Cargaa 1 EP for 7 April, with Marfox as its central figure. Three days later Revolução 2005–2008, a collection of tracks he made in his bedroom in those years, came out on CD and as a free download. One of his first international collaborations was a rework of tUnE-yArDs' "Water Fountain" featuring the Brazilian band Pearls Negras. His Chapa Quente EP includes "Tarraxo Everyday".

points.title: Where it started
points.text: In 2005 he founded DJs do Guetto with DJ Pausas and DJ Fofuxo. Their 37-track DJs do Ghetto Vol. I went up on eMule in 2006 and is seen as the founding release of the Lisbon ghetto sound.

points.title: Taking it global
points.text: In 2014 came Red Bull Music Academy in New York, Rolling Stone's "10 New Artists You Need to Know" and MoMA PS1's Warm Up on 30 August. In spring 2015 Warp's Cargaa 1 EP put him at its centre.

points.title: Start here
points.text: Eu sei quem Eu Sou (Príncipe Discos, 2011), which Philip Sherburne called "an atomic field of taut drums, hiccupping yelps, zapping synths and pinprick details." Then Subliminar (Enchufada, 2013), Revolução 2005–2008 and Chapa Quente.

headline: Tresor condemns Helsing AI military event at Kraftwerk
standfirst: Tresor has issued a statement condemning a military event held by Helsing AI at Kraftwerk Berlin.
body: Tresor has issued a statement condemning a military event held by Helsing AI at Kraftwerk Berlin.
The Berlin institution said such an event "has no place in the spaces our community has built".
The statement puts the club at odds with the use of a Berlin space closely linked to its community for an event tied to AI and the military.

headline: Arca, Justice and Fcukers land on the GTA VI album
standfirst: 'Grand Theft Auto VI: The Album' is out now and streaming, with Arca, Justice and Fcukers among the artists on the tracklist.
body: 'Grand Theft Auto VI: The Album' is out and available to listen to now. Arca, Justice and Fcukers are among the artists on it.
The LP comes right after the game's launch earlier this week. Grand Theft Auto VI had been a long time coming.
More artists appear on the album beyond those three. Arca, Justice and Fcukers are the names at the front of the coverage.
The release puts these artists, all familiar to people who follow electronic and club music, on the soundtrack album of one of the most anticipated games in years.

headline: CircoLoco gets its own radio station in GTA VI
standfirst: Grand Theft Auto VI launched worldwide this week, and its soundtrack includes CircoLoco Records Radio, hosted by Seth Troxler.
body: Grand Theft Auto VI came out worldwide this week, and club music has a big presence in it. One of its 22 radio stations is CircoLoco Records Radio. Seth Troxler hosts it, and it plays a batch of tracks that haven't been released yet.

The unreleased tracks are CHRIS STASSY's 'We On This Ride', DJ Tennis's 'Never Look Back' featuring Tomike, and 'I Feel Love' by Chloé Caillet & Myd. Also on the list: Mind Against's 'Let It Go', Carlita & Barker's 'Last Night', Troxler's own 'Bootlicker' and Rossi. & Demi's 'Deep N Sexy'. There are two remixes as well, Max Dean on Black Lounge's 'Bickering' and DJ Lag & Palms Trax on Rampa's 'The Church'. Released tracks by Michael Bibi, KETTAMA, PAWSA and Skream fill out the playlist.

There's more for club listeners. French duo Justice composed the game's original score. A hidden 23rd station called The Vault Radio reportedly unlocks once you find a poster inside The Vault, a fictional nightclub in downtown Vice City, and it plays the electronic mixes heard in that club. Gilles Peterson's Worldwide FM includes dubstep pioneer Mala, 4hero and the UK bass MC Magugu. Palms Trax and Burna Boy co-host AfroBank FM. Radio On-U takes its name from Adrian Sherwood's dub label On-U Sound. Flash FM includes Daft Punk and X-Press 2, and Robyn is one of its presenters.
The game also comes with a standalone 34-track album. Early reviews are overwhelmingly positive, and some critics already rank it among the best video games ever made.

The tie-in also carries over into real clubs. This weekend Miami's Club Space hosts a three-day takeover based on The Vault. Justice, Chris Lorenzo, Sammy Virji, Demi Riquísimo, DJ Tennis, Palms Trax, Seth Troxler and Skream are among the DJs playing.
Artists are already reacting. Max Dean and Black Lounge commented on DJ Mag's post that 'Bickering has been freed', and fans joked that the soundtrack will turn gamers into DJs.

points.title: A hidden club station
points.text: A 23rd station, The Vault Radio, reportedly unlocks when you find a poster inside The Vault, a fictional nightclub in downtown Vice City. It plays the club mixes heard inside the venue.

points.title: Selectors on the dial
points.text: Gilles Peterson hosts Worldwide FM, and Mala, 4hero and Magugu are on it. Palms Trax and Burna Boy front AfroBank FM. Radio On-U takes its name from Adrian Sherwood's dub label.

points.title: The Vault, for real
points.text: This weekend Miami's Club Space hosts a three-day takeover based on The Vault. Justice, Seth Troxler, DJ Tennis, Palms Trax, Skream, Sammy Virji and others are playing.

headline: Refuge NYC plans 63-hour NYE marathon with Tenaglia
standfirst: Refuge NYC will see in the New Year with ETERNIA, a dancefloor marathon that runs nonstop for 63 hours.
body: Refuge NYC is greeting the New Year with ETERNIA, a dancefloor marathon that will run for 63 hours without stopping.
Thirteen artists are booked across the event, drawn from house, techno and progressive music. Danny Tenaglia and Sasha lead the billing, and the rest of the lineup covers the same three genres.

The idea behind ETERNIA is an extended celebration, not a standard New Year's Eve party with a fixed closing time. With 63 hours to fill, the programme is built around one continuous dancefloor. The music keeps going from the countdown well into the days that follow.

The genre mix matters at that length. House, techno and progressive move at different energies and tempos, so booking across all three gives the run room to change mood over nearly three days instead of holding one pitch throughout.

Marathon formats like this ask something of the crowd as well as the DJs. Dancers can plan their own route through the weekend: arrive for a specific set, come back later, or try to stay as long as possible. Each person ends up with a different version of the party.

So far the published details are the format, the 63-hour length and the headline names. Set times, how the lineup is split across the run and ticketing information had not been included in the announcement.

headline: Korg phase8 gets free web app, firmware 1.3
standfirst: Korg's companion app for the phase8 acoustic synthesizer is now public. First shown at Superbooth in Berlin, it's free and runs in Chrome or Chromium browsers. Connect the phase8 over USB-C and it's ready to use.
body: Korg has released a free companion app for the phase8, its acoustic synthesizer, along with firmware version 1.3. The app was first shown at Superbooth in Berlin. It runs as a web application in Chrome and Chromium browsers: you plug the phase8 into a computer over USB-C and start working, with nothing to install.

The most obvious change is in the sequencer, which goes from 16 to 32 steps. The app also acts as a pattern editor and librarian. You can store patterns on your computer or on the instrument itself, and you can update the firmware from the same screen. Korg's Iarla Scaife in Berlin and Keisuke Nohara in Tokyo started the project, which adds on-screen tools for developing ideas so you're not working on the hardware alone.

This matters because the phase8 makes sound by physically exciting resonators, not with code. That has made it a talking point at a time when most music-making happens in software. Until now, the instrument offered limited ways to save and organise patterns. Being able to see a sequence on screen and keep a library of patterns makes it more practical in the studio and on stage.

Firmware 1.3 is available now. It fixes resonator behaviour that was sometimes unreliable, adds support for the companion app and improves sync and MIDI. Korg has published full release notes on its website.

Two other projects from Korg's Superbooth booth have no release plans yet: a set of custom bass resonators and a series of 3D-printed 'physical effects' by Hadrien Costrejean. Korg hasn't said whether either will be made more widely available.

points.title: What changes for you
points.text: phase8 owners can now write 32-step patterns, see their sequences on screen and back up their work to a computer. It costs nothing and needs only a browser and a USB-C cable.

points.title: Why update to 1.3
points.text: Firmware 1.3 fixes the resonators that sometimes behaved unpredictably and improves sync and MIDI. It's also required to use the new companion app.

points.title: Still unreleased
points.text: At Superbooth, Korg also showed custom bass resonators and 3D-printed 'physical effects' by Hadrien Costrejean. There's no word yet on whether either will get a wider release.

headline: Serato opens SoundSpace artist hub in Los Angeles
standfirst: Serato has opened SoundSpace, a 4,500-square-foot headquarters for DJs, producers and artists in Los Angeles' Arts District. It will host workshops and live showcases, and visiting artists can use the company's full product suite.
body: Serato has opened SoundSpace, a new headquarters for DJs, producers and artists in the Arts District of Los Angeles. The 4,500-square-foot site will host workshops and live showcases. Visiting artists get hands-on access to the company's full range of products.

The building has three main areas: a production studio, a tech library and a dedicated DJ space. The audio was designed by NNNN and OJAS. The DJ setup is built around two custom ON8 loudspeakers from the pair, and these are the first to use wide-dispersion multisectoral horns. It is also NNNN's first commercial installation in Los Angeles.

In the production studio, producers will work on NNNN's U15 nearfield monitoring system, which hasn't been released yet. The tech library holds a selection of Serato controllers and mixers for artists to try. Serato's Artist Relations team, made up of DJs, producers and audio engineers, will be on site to give technical support.
The space had its soft launch with DJ sets from The Alchemist, Novena Carmel and Jared Jackson.
Upcoming events include a private listening party with producer Dahi and workshops with Beatport, Kittens and Duckworld.

For working DJs and producers, the appeal is clear. SoundSpace mixes a showroom, a studio and a venue, with a sound system built specifically for the room and a monitoring setup that isn't available anywhere else yet.

points.title: The sound system
points.text: The DJ area runs two custom OJAS and NNNN ON8 loudspeakers, the first to use wide-dispersion multisectoral horns. It is also NNNN's first commercial installation in Los Angeles.

points.title: Inside the studio
points.text: The production studio uses NNNN's U15 nearfield monitoring system, which hasn't been released yet. The tech library holds a selection of Serato controllers and mixers.

points.title: What's next
points.text: Coming up are a private listening party with producer Dahi and workshops with Beatport, Kittens and Duckworld. Serato's Artist Relations team will give technical support on site.

headline: Sven Väth and Roman Flügel open Time Warp Records
standfirst: After more than three decades of throwing parties, Time Warp has started its own record label.
body: Time Warp has launched its own record label. The first release, catalogue number TWR001, is 'Rings of Light', a collaboration between Sven Väth and Roman Flügel.
The label comes after more than three decades of Time Warp events. Snippets of the record are available on Time Warp's official channel, so you can hear a preview before getting the full release.

Starting a catalogue at 001 shows the label has plans beyond a single record. Opening with a joint credit from Väth and Flügel ties the label's first release to two artists whose careers have both run alongside the party series. For now the material confirms only the title, the artists and the catalogue number. Nothing has been announced about formats, a tracklist, or what comes after TWR001.

Plenty of club and festival brands have turned their name into a label, using the reputation they built on the dancefloor to release music under their own banner. Time Warp is now doing the same, though with three decades of parties behind it. How the label develops will depend on who it signs next and whether it sticks with established names or makes space for newer producers.
For now, the 'Rings of Light' snippets are the first sound of the new label. HARDMAG will report details on the full release, formats and future catalogue numbers once they are confirmed.

headline: Kraftwerk Berlin apologises for hosting Helsing event
standfirst: Kraftwerk, the Berlin venue, has apologised for hosting an exhibition for Helsing, a company that makes AI weapons.
body: Kraftwerk, the Berlin venue, has apologised for hosting an exhibition for Helsing, a company that makes AI weapons.

Mixmag reported the story and said the venue was fitted out to look like a "military command post" for the event. Those are the only details of the set-up given so far. The report does not include the wording of Kraftwerk's apology, the date of the exhibition or what was on show.

The apology matters beyond one booking. Berlin's electronic music community sees its spaces as more than rooms for hire. Many people in the scene treat them as places with shared values, and they watch closely who uses them when the music stops. Seeing a venue linked to the city's club and arts world dressed as a military operations room for a weapons maker is bound to provoke a reaction.

The story also touches a debate that keeps growing: how artificial intelligence is moving from studios and streaming platforms into far less benign areas. HARDMAG follows AI in music closely, from production tools to rights and royalties. This case is a reminder that the same technology also powers businesses that many artists and ravers would not want to be associated with.

The questions left open are practical ones that every venue faces with private and corporate hire. Who decides which clients are acceptable? Is there any vetting before a contract is signed? And what does an apology change for future bookings?
HARDMAG will update this story if Kraftwerk or Helsing release more details about the event or the venue's response.

headline: DJ Ride wins DMC World Open title at London's KOKO
standfirst: DJ Ride has won the Open category at the 41st DMC World DJ Championships, held on Saturday at KOKO in London. It is his first DMC world title.
body: DJ Ride has won the Open category at the DMC World DJ Championships. He took the title on Saturday at KOKO in London, where the competition held its 41st edition, and it is his first DMC world title.

DMC has run since 1985 and is often called the Olympics of DJing. It is the best-known contest in turntablist culture, with a reputation for technical difficulty and inventive routines. Open competitors have to combine technique, musicality and creativity while building a set that works for the audience, all within 12 minutes.

Ride got to London by winning the Open category at DMC Iberia, held in Vigo in August. In a thank-you post on Instagram, he said he had wanted to be DMC world champion, and to earn the gold record and jacket, since the first time he touched a turntable. He described going from last place to first after many attempts and years of hard work. He also said part of his set was a love letter to British music, which he has been listening to since childhood, and added that he would have said more if the round weren't capped at 12 minutes.

The win adds to an already strong competition record. Ride holds four world titles from the International DJ Association (IDA). Two came in 2011 and 2016 as part of Beatbombers, his duo with Stereossauro. The other two were individual IDA titles in the Show and Technical categories in 2023.

Stereossauro won the DMC Open in 2024, so both halves of Beatbombers have now won the category. Ride's career spans hip-hop, electronic music and new approaches to turntablism, and this title makes him one of the leading competition DJs in the world.

points.title: From last to first
points.text: Ride says he wanted the DMC gold record and jacket from the first time he touched a turntable. He describes going from last place to first after years of attempts.

points.title: Fifth world title
points.text: He already holds four IDA world titles: two with Beatbombers in 2011 and 2016, plus individual Show and Technical titles in 2023.

points.title: A Beatbombers double
points.text: His Beatbombers partner Stereossauro won the DMC Open in 2024, so both members of the duo have now taken the category.

headline: Craig Richards plays his first all-night set at fabric
standfirst: Craig Richards will play open to close at fabric on Saturday, January 16th, 2027. It will be the first time in his 27-year residency at the London club that he plays the whole night alone.
body: Craig Richards is set to play his first open-to-close set at fabric on Saturday, January 16th, 2027. That's a first in the 27 years he has held a residency at the London club.

Richards has been a resident since fabric opened its doors in 1999. Through his selections and programming, he has had a central hand in shaping the club's musical identity over that time. He has played plenty of long sets in different rooms and formats, but he has never covered an entire night alone, from the moment the doors open until closing.
He's aware of how unusual that is. "After twenty-seven years and nearly eight hundred occasions, it's strange to think that I have never played alone for the duration of the night," Richards says.

On the night, Richards alone will control the music in Room One from start to finish. It's a new format for one of fabric's longest-serving residents, and it puts one DJ in charge of how the whole night is shaped and paced.

For a club whose identity is tied so closely to its residents, the date is a milestone for both the DJ and the venue. For anyone who has followed Richards' sets at fabric over the years, it's a rare chance to hear him play a full night in the room he helped define.

headline: Deezer study: 72% of listeners want AI music transparency
standfirst: In a new survey from Deezer, 72% of music streaming users said they want more transparency about AI-generated music on streaming platforms.
body: Most music streaming users want platforms to be clearer about AI-generated music. In a survey from Deezer, 72% of respondents said they want more transparency about AI music on streaming services.

The survey also found that many listeners don't realise they're already hearing it. Almost three-quarters of respondents believed their playlists had no AI-generated music, but 57% of respondents did have AI tracks on them.

That gap is the main finding. Most listeners say they care where their music comes from, but many can't tell when a track was made by AI. When AI music can sit on a playlist without anyone noticing, a label or tag may be the only way listeners can know what they're hearing.

This matters for the electronic music community. Producers, labels and DJs who build their work around streaming are now competing with AI-generated tracks that listeners often can't spot. Clear labelling would let listeners choose for themselves and would make it easier to see which music came from a human artist.

The figures come from Deezer's own survey, as reported by Mixmag. In short, most of the listeners surveyed want to know when music was made by AI, and many of them are already hearing it without knowing.

points.title: The perception gap
points.text: Almost three-quarters of respondents believed they had no AI tracks on their playlists. In fact, 57% did. Many listeners can't tell when they're hearing AI music.

points.title: Why it matters
points.text: Human producers are competing for the same playlist spots as AI tracks that listeners often can't spot. Most users surveyed say they want that made visible.

points.title: The ask
points.text: 72% of the streaming users surveyed want platforms to be more transparent about AI-generated music.

headline: Spotify vows to protect artists from misattributed AI tracks
standfirst: Spotify says it will "protect" artists from AI-generated tracks that are wrongly attributed to them, Mixmag reports.
body: Spotify says it will "protect" artists from AI-generated tracks that are misattributed to them, according to a report from Mixmag. The streaming giant is not stepping back from AI, though. AI use is still allowed on the platform, and Spotify is preparing to launch an AI remix service in 2027.

Those two moves sum up where the biggest streaming service now stands on machine-made music. It is promising artists some protection when their names are attached to AI tracks they had nothing to do with. At the same time, it is keeping its doors open to AI content and building its own AI product.

For DJs and producers in electronic music, misattribution is not an abstract worry. An artist's name on a streaming profile drives discovery, bookings and royalties, so a track wrongly credited to that name hits all three. Spotify's pledge is a public acknowledgement that the problem exists on its platform.

The planned remix service matters just as much. Remixing has long been one of the core crafts of club music. A platform-built AI tool for it raises clear questions for the producers whose work feeds that culture: who gets credited, who gets paid, and how much control original artists will have.
The report doesn't say how Spotify will carry out its protection pledge or how the 2027 remix service will work. HARDMAG will follow both as more details come out.

headline: Berlin Atonal condemns Kraftwerk over AI military event
standfirst: Berlin Atonal has publicly said it "strongly condemns" Kraftwerk, the former power station in Mitte that has long been its home, after the venue hosted an exhibition for an AI military firm.
body: Berlin Atonal has said it "strongly condemns" Kraftwerk, the former power station in Berlin's Mitte district where the festival is staged. The criticism follows the venue's decision to host an exhibition for an AI military firm.
In its statement, the festival said it "should not be housed in a space that goes against its values". That is unusually direct language from an event about the building it is identified with.
Even so, Atonal will return to Kraftwerk for its next edition. Based on what has been reported, the festival is objecting to the venue's choice of client without leaving the building.

For the club and festival community, the episode raises a question beyond Berlin. Large industrial venues often take on corporate and private bookings alongside cultural programming. Artists and promoters cannot always choose who else uses the spaces where their events take place.

The AI connection makes the story more pointed. AI is already changing how music is made and distributed, and its use in military technology is now an issue for one of electronic music's most closely watched festivals.
The festival's next edition at the former Mitte power station will be the first since the dispute.

points.title: Why it matters
points.text: It is rare for a festival to publicly criticise its own venue. The dispute links AI, the military and the spaces where electronic music happens.

points.title: The contradiction
points.text: Atonal says the festival should not be housed in a space that goes against its values. It is still returning to Kraftwerk for its next edition.

points.title: What to watch
points.text: The festival's next edition at the former Mitte power station will be the first since the dispute.

headline: Vilnius Nights: four clubs, one €10 ticket
standfirst: In 2026, Vilnius Days, the Lithuanian capital's 33-year-old street festival, extended into Vilnius Nights for the first time. Four nightclubs stayed open until 6AM, and one €10 ticket got you into all of them.
body: In 2026, Vilnius Days, the Lithuanian capital's 33-year-old street festival, extended into Vilnius Nights for the first time. Four nightclubs stayed open until 6AM, and one €10 ticket got you into all of them.

The Vilnius Night Office ran the initiative. The city municipality set up this public institution in 2023. It gives venues financial aid, offers staff training and mental health support, and runs harm reduction campaigns.
The event came months after Opium Club, open since 2009, closed in February. Mixmag also visited Draugų Vardai, an art and music space with a custom-built soundsystem.

headline: Tourism boom squeezes Reykjavík's music venues
standfirst: Tourism-driven gentrification is pushing Reykjavík's music venues out to make way for hotels and restaurants, artists and industry figures told Mixmag during Iceland Airwaves.
body: Tourism-driven gentrification is pushing Reykjavík's music venues out to make way for hotels and restaurants, artists and industry figures told Mixmag during Iceland Airwaves.

The festival's 27th edition ran across just seven spaces, including punk bar Lemmy, the Kolaport market hall, an independent church and City Hall. Producer Ida Juhl, aka knackered, says DIY crews host parties in bars they don't own: "pull up, build the stage and build the sound."
A newly formed Reykjavík Nighttime Industries Advocacy Group is now working to support and protect the city's venues.

headline: Mamdani names Eric Thor NYC nightlife director
standfirst: New York Mayor Zohran Mamdani has named Eric Thor Executive Director of the city's Office of Nightlife. Mamdani announced the appointment on Friday, November 13.
body: New York Mayor Zohran Mamdani has named Eric Thor Executive Director of the city's Office of Nightlife. Mamdani announced the appointment on Friday, November 13.

Thor was born in Queens and was previously lead developer at LaborLab, an organisation that supports unionisation. He will meet workers, business owners and community members across all five boroughs to shape the office's priorities, with a focus on working conditions and licensing.
“Nightlife is for everyone, from clubs to queer spaces to immigrant-run venues,” Thor said.

headline: Detroit to celebrate the life of Juan Atkins
standfirst: The family of Juan Atkins will host a public celebration of the electronic music pioneer's life and legacy on Sunday, November 22nd, at The Lincoln Factory in Detroit.
body: The family of Juan Atkins will host a public celebration of the electronic music pioneer's life and legacy on Sunday, November 22nd, at The Lincoln Factory in Detroit.
The 12-hour gathering is open to family, friends, fans and fellow artists. In its Instagram announcement, the family wrote: "All are welcome. Please celebrate his life and work with us."
Atkins died on November 1st in Mexico City, aged 64. His foundational role in Detroit techno helped establish a musical language that has shaped generations of producers and DJs worldwide.
